content: Phosphoprotein associated with glycosphingolipid-enriched microdomains 1 (PAG1) is a protein encoded by the PAG1 gene in humans. This protein functions as a type III transmembrane adaptor protein and has the ability to bind to the tyrosine kinase csk protein. It is believed to play a role in the regulation of T cell activation. PAG1 has been demonstrated to interact with several key proteins, including FYN, a member of the Src family of tyrosine kinases; C-src tyrosine kinase, another critical member of the Src family; Sodium-hydrogen antiporter 3 regulator 1 (NHERF1), which is involved in ion transport regulation; and the Abl gene product, a non-receptor tyrosine kinase implicated in various cellular processes.
